_doc: AUTHORED reading of Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20 for the background behind Prairie Avenue: Indiana Avenue's east frontage, 16th to 18th Street, and East Sixteenth Street's row at 209-217 (T-3019, piece 2 of T-3010, which tools/census_prairie_1904_background.py ranks: 12 of the block's 17 Indiana lots and the 16th Street lot are seen from Prairie's walks, 1623 from 13 stands). The T-1840 census (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/sheet_census/sheet-20.json) counts Prairie frontages only, so these rows are read here, in the same frontage contract, for tools/trace_prairie_1904_footprints.py (sheet '20w') and tools/draft_prairie_1904.py. Every lot is checked against Robinson 1886 plate 10, which covers this block. Where the two plans agree (209-217 E. 16th, 1615-1617, 1623, 1703, 1713, and the stables on 1637 and 1641) the 1911 outline is drafted for 1904. Where they disagree the frontage is ruled phase_unresolved and not drafted: the corner office and tin shop at 1601-1603, the ice-cream factory at 1605-1613, the photographic-supply factory at 1727-1737 (1886 houses, 1911 works), and 1619 (an 1886 frame house, a 1911 brick one). The 1886 brick houses on 1637 and 1641, gone by 1911, are not drafted either. T-3068 reads all of them. The six unnumbered strips (indiana_1623_1637_a and _b, indiana_1713_1727_a to _d) are open on both plans and are not traced.

comparison.how: The 1904 grid's parcel lines drawn over the plate through data/traces/gcp/robinson_1886_plate_10_gcps.json and read by eye at 3x; the plate is read for presence and material only, never for an outline.

reading.by: Read by eye from the committed sheet 20 scan (5879 x 7323 px), the 1904 grid's parcel lines drawn over each crop, 2026-10-23.
reading.conventions: Sanborn colour: pink brick, yellow frame, blue stone. A crossed square marks a stable. D = dwelling. Storey figures as printed (B = basement).
reading.limits: A 1911 label is a 1911 observation (study ruling 11): the office, the factories and the sheds' 1911 use are not carried back to 1904. Robinson 1886 is read for what stood on a lot and in what material, never for its outline. No dimension is claimed beyond the trace.

polygons.reading_1911: 5-storey brick building, 70 ft, across both numbers at the 16th Street corner, lettered OFFICE and TIN SHOP 5TH, an elevator inside; 201 E. 16th St. is printed on its cross-street side

frontages.why: Robinson 1886 plate 10 draws the corner as the west end of the brick row along 16th Street; the 1911 sheet draws a five-storey office and tin shop in its place. Nothing in hand dates the change: no named record, no 1904 directory row in the T-1837 study and no plan between the two. The 1911 use is not carried back (study ruling 11) and the 1886 building is not stood on a guess, so the frontage's 1904 phase is left open and the draft stands nothing here until T-3068 reads it.

polygons.reading_1911: A row of five 3½B brick dwellings (D), 209 to 217 E. 16th St., its four party walls carried to the row's rear wall, an open yard behind it to 1605's wall

frontages.why: No named record or 1904 directory row for this lot is in the T-1837 study. Robinson 1886 plate 10 and the 1911 sheet draw the same building on it, the brick row along East Sixteenth Street, its party walls at the same spacing, so it stood across the years either side of 1904: the draft stands the 1911 sheet's outline for 1904 as background, its presence inferred from the two plans (study ruling 11) under the block's single liberty. The row is drafted as one building, the sheet's one outline.
